> ## **1\. Project Overview & Scope**

> ### **1.1 Executive Summary**

FitFusion AI is a standalone web application that delivers an interactive 2D virtual try-on and outfit simulation experience with a mock e-commerce flow. It addresses the pre-purchase uncertainty problem documented in the Project Charter (P1, P3) — shoppers cannot judge how a garment will look on their body type, skin tone, and personal style before buying — and the retailer-side returns problem (P4). The MVP reduces this uncertainty through (a) multi-angle visualization of catalog garments on a personalized avatar and (b) explainable, rule-based style/color recommendations powered by a deterministic Heuristic Expert System (symbolic/heuristic AI, not ML). A simulated purchase workflow is provided through a standalone mock payment gateway to validate the e-commerce UX without real-money risk.

The system is built on a React (+Vite) frontend, a Python 3.13+ / Django 6.x REST backend with JWT authentication and server-side RBAC, and a MongoDB Atlas cloud database. The application itself runs on a dedicated local staging host; only the database remains cloud-hosted (Charter §6.1.8, Scope §1.5).

> ### **1.2 System Scope**

> #### ***In-Scope (Charter §4.1 / Scope §1.1)***

1. **Authentication & RBAC:** JWT-based registration/login with role selection (Registered User / Guest / Seller), password policy enforcement (FR-1.5), server-side RBAC, and ephemeral Guest sessions (FR-1.8, FR-1.9).  
2. **Multi-Angle Avatar System:** Male and Female avatars customizable via Height and Body Build sliders (height 120–220 cm; Body Build 86–112 cm), skin tone, undertone, and simulation-only body-proportion categories (shoulder, waist, hip, thigh, female-only cup size). Body Build is driven by a deterministic BMI-derived silhouette mapping (BMI proxy 21–32 mapped onto 86–112 cm) for visual simulation only; the ranges and the S–4XL size ladder (each size step adds 4 cm of Body Build girth, with 4XL clamped at the 112 cm validated ceiling) are design bounds informed by DOST-FNRI anthropometric averages and common Asian retail sizing assumptions (Charter §6.1.14, \[R19\]). When a garment size is equipped, the Height/Body Build controls are constrained to the size-compatible sub-range, with the global ranges as outer bounds (FR-2.3). Procedural client-side deformation of a single base silhouette per gender. Front and Rear views (FR-2.1–2.10).  
3. **Seller-Managed Catalog:** CSV-only upload pipeline (proprietary spreadsheet formats XLSX/XLS/ODS are excluded) with two labeled drop zones (Front / Rear), automated rembg background removal, Pillow-based validation (rules a–e, including controlled-vocabulary conformance for categories and style tags), GridFS storage, and descriptive rejection reports (FR-4.1–4.8).  
4. **Virtual Try-On 2D Overlay Canvas:** Per-category item switching, instant Front/Rear view toggling, Dress/One-Piece replaces Top+Bottom slots, saved outfit CRUD (FR-5.1–5.8).  
5. **Explainable Rule-Based Styling Engine:** Deterministic Heuristic Expert System using weighted tag scoring — color compatibility (+3), height-appropriate contrast (+2), proportion-appropriate shading (+1), style tag match (+1) — with fully visible match reasons. Style tags are drawn from the controlled vocabulary (casual, smart, formal, sporty); non-vocabulary values are rejected at upload validation (FR-3.2, FR-4.7(a)). The optional in-app rating UI (FR-7.5) is deferred to post-MVP; MVP acceptance of the engine relies on panel observation of explainable match reasons (FR-7.3/7.4).  
6. **Mock E-Commerce Flow:** Persistent cart for Registered Users, full checkout UI, standalone in-Django mock payment gateway, and order history with per-item store names (FR-6.1–6.9).  
7. **Catalog Browsing & Filtering:** Filters by category, size, and price, plus per-seller Store pages listing all active items from each Seller (FR-3.3).

> #### ***Out-of-Scope (Charter §4.2 / Scope §1.4)***

1. Real payment processing and merchant fulfillment (mock only).  
2. User-uploaded photos or clothing images (Sellers only manage the catalog).  
3. Garment-fit prediction, size prediction, or fit guarantees — the system provides fit *visualization* only.  
4. All custom-trained Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Generative AI models. The in-scope recommender is a deterministic rule-based Heuristic Expert System (symbolic/heuristic AI); off-the-shelf utilities (rembg, Pillow) are permitted only as fixed preprocessing components.  
5. Fully 3D rotatable avatars, WebGL rendering, and dynamic cloth physics.  
6. Multi-seller marketplace discovery (Shopee-like); external third-party API integrations.  
7. Body tracking, pose detection, and fabric simulation.  
8. Cloud-hosted application hosting — only MongoDB Atlas remains cloud-hosted.  
9. Children's and infant clothing categories and pediatric body-proportion modeling; avatar inputs outside the validated ranges of 120–220 cm height and 86–112 cm Body Build.  
10. Anthropometric or tailoring accuracy claims for body-proportion category brackets (shoulder, waist, hip, cup size, thigh). These categories are simulation-only deformation controls; no real-world measurement or fit conclusion is derived from them.  
11. Native iOS/Android apps; multi-language localization (English only).  
12. Seller-side order management and fulfillment views — mock-checkout orders appear only in the purchasing user's order history, never in the Seller Dashboard (FR-6.9).  
13. Inventory/stock tracking, stock visibility to shoppers, and post-purchase logistics (delivery, shipping, packing, returns processing); the mock e-commerce flow ends at checkout simulation and order-history recording.  
14. Style tags outside the controlled vocabulary (casual, smart, formal, sporty), and proprietary spreadsheet formats (XLSX, XLS, ODS) for Seller catalog uploads.  
15. Automated in-app rating UI and the UAT survey instrument for Criteria 9–11 (deferred to post-MVP; MVP measurement is panel observation of functional delivery and explainable match reasons).

> ## **2\. System Architecture**

> ### **2.1 High-Level Architecture Overview**

FitFusion AI follows a **modular monolith** client-server architecture with three logical tiers and a staging-edge reverse proxy:

* **Presentation Layer (Client Tier):** A single React \+ Vite single-page application served by the staging proxy. Contains the avatar canvas, catalog browser, recommendation panel, cart/checkout UI, outfit manager, and Seller Dashboard.  
* **Application / Business Layer (Backend Tier):** A Django 6.x REST API served by Waitress (WSGI) on the local staging host. Houses authentication/RBAC, avatar preset management, catalog browsing, Seller upload & validation pipeline, recommendation engine, mock e-commerce module, ratings, and GridFS media serving.  
* **Data Layer:** MongoDB Atlas (free tier M0) for persistent documents (users, Sellers, catalog items, avatar presets, saved outfits, carts, orders, upload batches, ratings) and GridFS for transparent PNG garment images produced by rembg.  
* **Staging Edge (Reverse Proxy):** A Node.js HTTPS server terminates TLS (via mkcert local CA) on port 8443, serves the built React files statically, and proxies API paths over loopback HTTP to Django at 127.0.0.1:8000. This is the only component that faces the browser; everything downstream is on the same local machine.

**Single external dependency:** MongoDB Atlas is the only cloud-hosted service. All application computers runs on the local staging host, eliminating vendor lock-in and third-party approval delays during the semester (Charter §6.1.8, Scope §1.5).

**Known limitation (2D overlay alignment):** because clothing overlays are pre-processed 2D PNGs layered over a procedurally deformed base silhouette, minor alignment deviation or transient visual artifacts may appear at extreme body-proportion combinations or during rapid view switching. This is inherent to photo-based 2D overlay visualization and is not treated as a functional defect provided the alignment-grid registration and the Criterion 2 rendering target (\<1 s) are met (Charter §6.1.13; SRS §2.4; Scope §1.6).

> ### **2.3 Architectural Components Description**

| Component | Technology | Responsibilities | Traceability |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Presentation Layer (Frontend)** | React 18+ with Vite, HTML5 Canvas API, standard CSS | Render the avatar canvas with procedural client-side silhouette deformation; layer transparent PNG garments; handle Front/Rear view toggling; implement catalog browsing, filters, per-seller Store page; provide cart/checkout UI; surface recommendation panel with match reasons (rating controls deferred to post-MVP per FR-7.5); deliver the Seller Dashboard with CSV template download, two-drop-zone upload, listings management, and validation reports. | SRS §5.1; WBS 1.2.3, 1.3.2, 1.3.4, 1.3.8 |
| **Application / Business Layer (Backend)** | Python 3.13+, Django 6.x, Django REST Framework, SimpleJWT, Waitress (WSGI) | JWT-based registration/login with role assignment (FR-1.1); server-side RBAC enforcement on every protected endpoint (FR-1.7); avatar preset CRUD scoped to owner (FR-2.5–2.10); CSV \+ image upload pipeline with rembg background removal, Pillow-based validation rules a–e, and GridFS storage (FR-4.1–4.8); deterministic weighted scoring recommendation service (FR-7.1–7.5); mock payment gateway service (FR-6.5); cart/checkout/order endpoints (FR-6.1–6.8); rating API endpoints (FR-7.5 — backend implemented; the frontend rating UI and UAT rating/survey capture are deferred to post-MVP, so MVP acceptance relies on panel observation of explainable match reasons); account deactivation \+ restricted archival (FR-1.4, RA 10173); controlled-vocabulary validation (categories per FR-3.1; style tags casual/smart/formal/sporty per FR-3.2) and CSV-only file-type guard (FR-4.1/4.7). | SRS §3, §5.2; WBS 1.3.1, 1.3.3, 1.3.5–1.3.8 |
| **Data Layer** | MongoDB Atlas M0 (cloud), GridFS for media | Persistent document storage for users, Sellers (with Store Name), catalog items, avatar presets, saved outfits (with inline avatar snapshots), carts, orders (with item snapshots), upload batches, and ratings. GridFS stores the rembg-generated transparent PNG garment images and serves them via the Django media endpoint. | SRS §5.2; ERD (see §3.1) |
| **Staging Edge — Node.js HTTPS Reverse Proxy** | Node.js 20+, native `https` module, mkcert local CA | Terminates TLS 1.2+ on port 8443 for the staging demonstration URL; serves the built React `dist/` files as static assets; proxies API paths (`/auth/`, `/catalog/`, `/cart/`, `/orders/`, `/presets/`, `/outfits/`, `/ratings/`, `/api/`, `/media/`, etc.) over loopback HTTP to Django at 127.0.0.1:8000. Does not implement business logic — it is a pure transport \+ static-serving layer. | SRS §5.3; Charter §6.1.8; WBS 1.5.1 |
| **Mock Payment Gateway (internal service)** | Pure Python service inside the Django backend (`commerce/services.py`) | Simulates payment approval/decline for checkout without real money, external APIs, or regulatory exposure. Deterministic: approves unless the payment-method string contains "decline". Returns a synthetic transaction reference on approval. | SRS FR-6.5; Charter §4.2 item 1 |
| **External Services** | MongoDB Atlas (only external dependency) | Atlas M0 free tier provides the cloud database. All connections use TLS (implied by `mongodb+srv://`). IP allowlist maintained per team member; hardening query parameters (`maxIdleTimeMS`, bounded timeouts, retries) configured in the connection string. | SRS §2.3, §4.2; Charter §6.1.5 |

## **6\. Appendices & References**

> ### **6.1 Glossary**

| Term / Acronym | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| SRS | Software Requirements Specification |
| SADD | System Architecture & Design Document |
| API | Application Programming Interface |
| RBAC | Role-Based Access Control — enforced server-side by Django on every protected endpoint (FR-1.7) |
| CRUD | Create, Read, Update, Delete — the four basic data-management operations |
| MVP | Minimum Viable Product — the Semester 1 deliverable using 2D avatars, mock e-commerce, and a rule-based recommender |
| CSV | Comma-Separated Values — file format used by Sellers to upload catalog items in bulk |
| PNG | Portable Network Graphics — image format with transparency, used for clothing overlays and avatar layers |
| JSON | JavaScript Object Notation — data format exchanged between frontend and backend |
| JWT | JSON Web Token — stateless authentication token issued by Django (SimpleJWT) |
| TLS | Transport Layer Security — TLS 1.2+ required for all external-facing traffic (SRS §4.2, §5.3) |
| WSGI | Web Server Gateway Interface — the standard Python interface between a web server (Waitress) and a Django application |
| GridFS | MongoDB's file-storage specification used to store rembg-processed transparent PNG garment images |
| Atlas | MongoDB Atlas — the cloud-hosted database service (M0 free tier) used by the system |
| rembg | Off-the-shelf Python library used for automated background removal; permitted as a fixed preprocessing component (not ML for recommendation) |
| Pillow (PIL) | Python Imaging Library used for image validation (dimensions, alpha channel, dominant-color extraction) |
| Body Build | A visual torso girth parameter (validated range 86–112 cm) used solely to deform the 2D base silhouette. The frontend employs a BMI-Derived Silhouette Mapping: it computes a visual ratio (weight\_kg / height\_m²) and maps a BMI proxy range of 21–32 onto the 86–112 cm spectrum, strictly clamped to the safe limits of the 2D asset mesh. Used solely for visual simulation — never for health, tailoring, or medical assessment (SRS §1.3, §2.4; Charter §6.1.14). |
| Controlled Vocabulary (Style Tags) | The fixed set of style tags accepted by the catalog: casual, smart, formal, sporty. Chosen as an MVP design bound spanning everyday / smart-casual / formal / active dress codes (no universal style taxonomy exists); keeps the \+1 style-match rule deterministic and explainable and Seller tagging simple. Values outside this set are rejected at upload validation (FR-3.2, FR-4.7(a)); extension is post-MVP. |
| Design Bounds | The supported avatar input ranges and S–4XL size grading are design assumptions informed by DOST-FNRI anthropometric averages and common Asian retail sizing — not certified anthropometric or tailoring standards (Charter §6.1.14). |
| Heuristic Expert System | The deterministic, rule-based recommender (symbolic/heuristic AI) that encodes color theory and style rules into explicit rules and weighted tag scoring — not a trained ML model |
| Fit Visualization vs. Fit Prediction | Fit visualization \= showing how a catalog garment looks on a personalized avatar (in-scope). Fit prediction \= claiming a size or physical-fit outcome (out-of-scope). The MVP provides visualization only. |
| WCAG | Web Content Accessibility Guidelines — target Level AA compliance (SRS §4.4) |
| RA 10173 | Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Philippines) — governs account deletion via deactivation \+ restricted archival (FR-1.4) |
| Loopback | The 127.0.0.1 network address used between the Node.js proxy and Django; traffic never leaves the staging host |
| mkcert | Local Certificate Authority tool used to issue trusted TLS certificates for the staging demonstration URL |
